statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail), and r is the least integer k >= 0 for which there exist k nonempty, pairwise disjoint index sets S_1,...,S_k whose union is {0,1,...,len(nums)-1} and such that, for each j, if the elements of S_j are written in increasing order i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{m-1}, then nums[i_0] < nums[i_1] < ... < nums[i_{m-1}]. Equivalently, r is the minimum number of operations required to delete all elements when each operation deletes a strictly increasing subsequence of the current array.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r equals the maximum length m of a non-increasing subsequence of nums, defined as indices i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{m-1} with 0 <= i_0, i_{m-1} < len(nums), and nums[i_0] >= nums[i_1] >= ... >= nums[i_{m-1]}. Since nums is nonempty, this maximum is at least 1.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 1 <= r <= len(nums).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r (an i64) and does not fail; there is no overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 1 if and only if for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums)-1, nums[i] < nums[i+1], equivalently the entire array is strictly increasing.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = len(nums) if and only if for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums)-1, nums[i] >= nums[i+1], equivalently nums is non-increasing so that for all i < j, nums[i] >= nums[j].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer v, r >= count(v), where count(v) is the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exist indices i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{r-1} with 0 <= i_0, i_{r-1} < len(nums), and nums[i_0] >= nums[i_1] >= ... >= nums[i_{r-1}]; that is, nums has a non-increasing subsequence of length exactly r.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exist r strictly increasing subsequences of nums whose index sets are pairwise disjoint and whose union is {0,1,...,len(nums)-1}.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer k with 0 <= k < r, there does not exist a partition of {0,1,...,len(nums)-1} into k nonempty index sets each of which, when sorted, gives a strictly increasing subsequence of nums.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every p with 1 <= p <= len(nums), the minimum number of strictly increasing subsequences needed to cover the prefix nums[0], nums[1], ..., nums[p-1] is at most r.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every s with 0 <= s < len(nums), the minimum number of strictly increasing subsequences needed to cover the suffix nums[s], nums[s+1], ..., nums[len(nums)-1] is at most r.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, let m be the minimum number of strictly increasing subsequences needed to cover the proper prefix nums[0], nums[1], ..., nums[len(nums)-2]. Then r <= m + 1.
preconditions: 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, let L be the maximum length of a strictly increasing subsequence of nums, i.e. the maximum m for which there exist indices i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{m-1} with 0 <= i_0, i_{m-1} < len(nums) and nums[i_0] < nums[i_1] < ... < nums[i_{m-1}]. Then r <= len(nums) - L + 1.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.
